[EXCEL] Weekend Notes: How much would you save in a year by drinking beer-flavored beverages with a 42-yen price difference? ~Daily Excel~
My two-year stint working away from home has ended, and I returned home this April (2026/R8).
I have beer in stock at home. It's from the hometown tax program.
[EXCEL] The deadline for hometown tax points is approaching, and I'm struggling with what to order. It's beer or nothing, though. ~Daily Excel~
The lowest price at the supermarket is 145 yen (excluding tax).

Since I had been drinking "Asahi Zero" before that, my tongue might have gotten used to the taste of non-alcoholic drinks, but although there are differences in harshness depending on the product, it doesn't bother me that much.
The price difference between "Dry Zero" and "Greens Free" is about 40 yen.
The tax-included price is calculated as tax-excluded price x 1.08.
A table like this can probably be made in 5 to 10 minutes.
I set them using "Conditional Formatting." Please see below for details (I think it's a pretty good idea, but it doesn't seem to be very popular...).
If you use the same bottle for four days, it's pretty flat by the end.

If I'm going to drink carbonated water, I suppose there's the option of a carbonation server, but I don't have the space for it, and it would probably be a hassle. You'd have to wash the bottles and things like that, right?
Annual price difference based on what you drink on weekdays (Monday to Thursday)
Since I started checking only once a month, I've been able to see how it grows. Since I've decided on 30,000 yen per month, there are no surprises.
It's easier to keep going when there are no surprises. If you look at something that fluctuates every day, your attention gets caught up in it.

I'm afraid to touch something that has been going on for three years. This isn't about logic. If a month comes where I actually set it to 40,000 yen and can't make the transfer, I'll probably quit everything right there.
I still don't know if it's better not to increase it. The fact that it reached 2 million yen in 3 years is probably not solely due to the 30,000 yen.
